newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche - may shed activities failing new benchmark.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche - may shed activities failing new benchmark.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Tuesday it had introduced a new performance measure with which to assess its 31 business areas and may shed activities if they do not live up to it.
"The modern universal bank bearing our name will no longer offer every product everywhere and at any time," Kopper told the bank's annual shareholders meeting.

Deutsche therefore aimed to find a new and more up-to-date weighting of its potential. This would be crucial in competition with its established competitors, particularly with non-banks and so-called "near-bank" rivals, Kopper said.

"We will need to examine whether the 31 business and service units in which we currently operate and to which we allocate valuable resources make the necessary, sustainable contribution to the group's overall strategy."
"After all, one is quicker and more agile with a lighter load."

Kopper said the bank now attached great importance to a new ratio for the medium-term optimisation of its profit potential. It is called "risk-adjusted return on capital" and is based on the return on the economic capital needed to cover the respective risks.

He added that Deutsche's aggregate targets still applied -- to increase its return on equity before tax to 25 percent and the cost-income ratio to well below 70 percent by the end of the century from respective 1996 levels of 17.1 percent and 71.7 percent.
